B.explanation: This is the percentage uncertainty in one side only, $0.1/30.0 \times 100\%$, before allowing for $V = L^3$.

C.explanation: Three times the side percentage uncertainty gives $3 \times 0.33\% = 1\%$ for $V = L^3$.

D.explanation: Too large. It may come from misreading $0.1$ mm as $1$ mm or misplacing the decimal in the percentage.

walkthrough: Identify the given data: length $L = 30.0\text{ mm}$ with absolute uncertainty $\Delta L = 0.1\text{ mm}$.
State the rule for one quantity: percentage uncertainty $= \Delta L / L \times 100\%$.
Substitute: $(0.1 / 30.0) \times 100\% = 0.333...\%$, the uncertainty in one side.
State the volume rule: $V = L \times L \times L = L^3$, so percentage uncertainties add.
Check units cancel to leave $\%$ and the result matches the $1\%$ option. This is option C.
